final.title: Anonymise before you automate
final.body:
Before you automate a workflow, make one decision first: does any document entering the process still contain customer identifiers? If yes, pause the build and strip or mask those details in a sample before you test AI on it. That applies to quotes, invoices, contracts, case notes, and summary slides as well. A system is only as clean as the input you give it.

If you run a small business, the practical check is simple. Pick one recurring workflow you already handle in email, CRM, a shared drive, or a Zapier/Make step. Then ask: where does the document first leave your control, and where does human review still happen? If review is already part of the path, keep it. If the workflow depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample first and use that for testing.

This is not an AI feature and not legal advice. It is a governance choice the owner makes before any automation gets near the file. Once the sample is clean, you have a better basis for deciding whether automation fits at all.

final.title: Anonymise first, automate second
final.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, make one decision first: does any document in that flow still contain customer identifiers? If the answer is yes, do not feed the raw sample into AI. Mask or remove names, emails, amounts, contract details, and anything else that would let a person be identified, then test with the cleaned version instead.

That matters most in the ordinary places a small business already works: email, CRM, shared drives, and tools like Zapier or Make. The question is not “can we automate this?” It is “what leaves our control, and where does human review still sit?” If a step already needs a person to check it, keep that checkpoint. If the workflow depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample before you experiment.

This is not legal advice, and it is not an AI feature. It is a governance rule the owner applies before any build. The clean sample does not remove your obligations, but it does make the next automation decision a lot less messy.
